metadata.description: Skills for working with clauz3 — using installed trusted layers, authoring new ones, and stress-testing agents through clauz3.

plugins.name: clauz3
plugins.description: For agents that need to do real-world things — send mail, edit files, fetch URLs, move money, run a lab step — in a project where clauz3 is the only outlet to side effects. Covers writing the small Python program against trusted modules, attaching guarantees the user will review, and passing through clauz3 prove / clauz3 run.

plugins.name: clauz3-authoring
plugins.description: For designing the trusted boundary an agent acts through — effects, contracts, fluents — when no trusted layer exists yet for a domain. Root-of-trust role: if this layer is wrong, every proof against it is wrong. Covers effects.py with deal/clauz3 markers, contracts via the relation algebra, optional fluents for stateful properties, and packaging as a clauz3-install-able library.

plugins.name: clauz3-exploring
plugins.description: For acting as the user-proxy while driving an independent Claude Code (or other agent) through clauz3 tasks adaptively — picking prompts, watching what the agent submits, deciding approvals via the approval service's REST API, escalating to adversarial cases, and surfacing design issues. Open-ended counterpart to the deterministic e2e driver.
